findings.claim: When StatedInteractionChips collapses two rule chips about one combination order (one per constituent), the surviving chip keeps only its own constituent's partner rows. So an answer naming one constituent is credited with naming the whole combination order, and an answer naming the other constituent is not. Which constituent counts depends on dataset order.
findings.evidence: A throwaway test in the reference package, since deleted, used OneOrderNameAcrossOneResponseTest's fixture (ddi-combination-two-rules-one-note.json, order 'Emtricitabine / Tenofovir disoproxil', question 'Can I give her bedaquiline?') and drove the real validate(). It returned 1 chip, partners=[Emtricitabine / Tenofovir disoproxil], rowsOfPartner=[300195 Tenofovir disoproxil] only. namesThePartner('...her tenofovir disoproxil [1].')=true and namesThePartner('...her emtricitabine [1].')=false. isFirstStatementOf (StatedInteractionChips) drops the second chip before any row union. The PR unions rows only in collapseSharedMechanisms (DrugSafetyValidator.java:4779-4815). StatedInteractionChips' javadoc says 'It removes a chip and nothing else', but the collapse now also decides findingPartners.stated and the appended sentence. ADR Decision 100's amendment ('a merged chip the union of its members'') does not mention this collapse. Recommended fix: attach partner rows only where the chip names the partner by an ENTRY label (the #555 shape), not on the ORDER rung where the printed name is her own prescription display. Containment already handles that display the way it did before this PR. Alternative: union the collapsed chip's rows into the survivor.

verdict: Mergeable. The change fixes #555 the way the reference CLAUDE.md requires: it uses the matchesText prose rule over rows carried structurally from the chip, mirroring namesTheFindingsSubject/findingSubjectRows from #515. The one gap is a non-blocking inconsistency for collapsed combination-order chips that errs toward reporting.
what_i_swept: Read the issue, the PR body, the full production diff and the test diff, plus the root CLAUDE.md and the reference CLAUDE.md in full. Confirmed git diff main...HEAD is 15 files, +493/-69, with no drift against the base. Solution fit: compared the change with the issue's proposed fix in comparable(), which the PR rejected for CLAUDE.md's 'Matching a drug name' rule. Compared it with its sibling precedents, namesTheEndedOrderDrug and namesTheFindingsSubject, and it matches both. Outward trace: (1) every SafetyWarning copy method carries partnerRows (asAboutAnEndedOrder, withMatchedOrderNames, withCurrentOrderDisplays, asStatedInTheAnswer, aboutSubstance); (2) namedPartners() equals singleton(partnerName) for the drug-in-play arm and chipPartnerName for the screening arm (interactionWarning at DrugSafetyValidator.java:7644), so the row map keys line up with the printed partners; (3) class-only, question-pair, contraindication and overdose chips have no namedPartners, so they are outside the population; (4) RecordMapping does not reach omod: grep returned zero hits, with a positive control on ChartAnswer; (5) the StatedInteractionChips collapse, which produced F1; (6) the module-answer path at LlmInferenceService:921. Tests: ran CitedFindingPartnerCompletionTest (14), ProjectInstructionsGuardTest (9), ArchitectureGuardTest (30), InteractionClaimPairFidelityTest (62) and SharedMechanismChipCollapseTest (7), all green at head. Mutation: removing withPartnerRows from collapseSharedMechanisms' merged chip reddened exactly anOrderOfAMergedFindingTheAnswerNamedWithoutItsLabelsParentheticalIsNotListedAgain, which confirms the PR's coverage claim for the merge site. Restored with git checkout; porcelain is clean.

I did not mutate the screening-arm or drug-in-play-arm write sites or namesThePartner individually. I relied on the PR's own mutation report for those, and independently confirmed only the merge site.

notes: Pass 1 found F1 through the outward trace into StatedInteractionChips. Pass 2 checked the copy sites, the wire reach and the merge-site mutation, and found nothing new.
